Hypothesis evaluation plays a significant role in cognitive science, where Bayes factors can compare and contrast competing theories by assessing their consistency with available data. However, implementing Bayes factor analysis is often complicated and heavily dependent on the accuracy of computational methods, as well as the choice of prior distributions and the specification of the model. To address these challenges, we was forced to develop an extensive cognitive science model to be able to test our research methods. Moreover, due to the notational complexities of Bayes factor analysis, multiple Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulations are typically required to acquire Bayes factor estimates, which can be difficult to set up and run successfully. To address these issues, we outline a step-by-step guide on how to conduct Bayes factor analysis and provide three reliable computational workflows for evaluating hypotheses in cognitive science using Bayes factors. The first workflow compares the fit of two simple models to available data, while the second and third workflows compare the fit of more complex models to available data by applying partial Bayes factor analysis. The third workflow also examines the source of Bayes factor instability by testing the effect of varying prior parameters on Bayes factor estimates. To facilitate the use of Bayes factors in cognitive science, we make our R code available on GitHub to be used by researchers.
